source.title: Coping with pain among adults with chronic tic disorders
source.license: CC BY 4.0, verified publisher copyright and Crossref license metadata

design.type: Cross-sectional convenience-sample questionnaire and interview study; no assigned intervention or comparator
design.population: Current attendees of adult tic-disorder support groups in several Polish locations; available willing members in July 2023
design.eligibility: Age at least 18 and neurologist diagnosis of GTS or CMTD under DSM-5
design.diagnostic_verification_limit: Prior neurologist diagnosis specified; independent re-diagnosis or chart verification not described
design.timing: Paper questionnaires without time limit; online one-to-one YGTSS interview within one week
design.followup: No longitudinal outcome follow-up; retrospective worst pain and recalled care
design.sample_size_basis: Available willing members, no a priori power calculation
design.participant_flow: Number invited, refusals, partial responders and outcome-specific missingness not reported
design.severe_persistence: No verified severe-adult subgroup, severity-duration criterion or continuous severe-persistence classification

instruments.name: Polish YGTSS
instruments.construct: Reported 0–100 combined tic severity and daily impairment score, not an isolated 0–50 total tic score
instruments.timing: Interview within one week of questionnaires; interview rating recall window not explicitly stated in this report
instruments.limits: Component tic and impairment scores not reported separately; pain association does not isolate pure tic severity

instruments.name: VAS
instruments.construct: Self-rated present and recalled worst tic-related pain, 0–10
instruments.timing: Present versus worst; worst-pain look-back period not specified, no average/typical-pain window
instruments.limits: Neither elapsed time nor repeat prospective follow-up; cannot interpret contrast as temporal worsening/improvement or treatment response

instruments.name: Polish SF-MPQ-2
instruments.construct: Continuous, intermittent, neuropathic-descriptor and affective pain dimensions
instruments.limits: Version citation, item denominator and domain-score computation inadequately specified. Table 5 percentages cannot be assumed within-gender prevalence. No clinically confirmed neuropathic mechanism or validated pain-interference endpoint follows from descriptors

instruments.name: Polish CSQ
instruments.construct: Seven coping strategies plus distinct 0–6 subjective pain-control and ability-to-reduce-pain items
instruments.limits: Strategy use does not show effectiveness; no causal recommendation or moral judgment about coping

instruments.name: Polish BPCQ
instruments.construct: Belief in own control, physicians and chance
instruments.limits: Belief is not actual treatment efficacy. Item counts, subscale maximums and normalization not specified; comparing raw subscale totals requires verified scoring

instruments.name: Study care-seeking survey, Appendix Part II
instruments.construct: Recalled professional/therapeutic help, provider/treatment choices, perceived usefulness, reasons for lack of success
instruments.supplement_checked: Both rendered pages of blank questionnaire inspected
instruments.response_options: Help-seeking and relief items each permit yes, no, and uncertain/cannot remember; provider, treatment and reasons permit multiple answers
instruments.timing: No bounded recall window or minimum duration of relief specified
instruments.limits: No per-treatment denominator, dose, timing, adherence, counterfactual or published counts for uncertain responses. Non-positive responses must not all be recoded as treatment failures

pain_counts.interpretation: Sample proportion endorsing past-or-present pain, not current prevalence, chronic-pain prevalence, representative adult population prevalence or severity distribution

ygtss.warning: Overall SD 16.00 is incompatible with the displayed complete sex partition; no corrected SD adopted

help_seeking.relief_duration: Narrative says reported effects temporary or insufficient; no numeric duration or separate durable-benefit count
help_seeking.provider_denominators: Not reliably defined. Multiple choices allowed, percentages are not disjoint categories. Do not infer counts or divide by asserted seekers without explicit assumptions
conflicts: 19+31=50, not the rounded86% of 56 under conventional rounding
31 women seeking help exceeds30 women in the pain subgroup
10 relief reports yield17.86% of 56 but20% of50; neither establishes18% of seekers

negative_and_counterevidence: No nominal gender difference for present or worst VAS overall or by diagnosis (Table 3); nonsignificance is not equivalence.
No reported significant pain-intensity differences by self-reported depression. Depression was not clinically screened in this study, and subgroup sample sizes are not supplied.
Only three of twelve Table 4 coefficients are marked nominally significant; female-GTS worst pain coefficient0.153 is unmarked, despite broad prose emphasizing women with GTS.
No reported association between coping strategies and YGTSS; no reported association between BPCQ beliefs and current or worst pain.
No nominal gender difference across the four reported SF-MPQ-2 domain comparisons or three BPCQ comparisons.
No participant reported complete subjective ability to reduce pain in section 8; this differs from the separately measured complete control item.
Care reports cannot show that professional care fails causally, nor that self-management is superior; no treatment allocation or longitudinal comparator exists.

other_aggregate_summaries.sf_mpq2_warning: Values preserved as reported, not revalidated person-level means. Item cells omitted because exact denominator/number of endorsers is uncertain and to avoid possible singleton reconstruction.
other_aggregate_summaries.csq_warning: Reported nominal associations; no multiplicity adjustment described, U/p consistency not resolved, no causal or general gender claims

reporting_concerns.issue: Help-seeking counts and percentages inconsistent, plus impossible female subset count; corrected denominator unknown
Displayed overall mean 4.3 incompatible with weighted diagnosis-specific means 4.6 and 4.2 using 20/10; rounding does not reconcile them
ADHD count 10 labelled 7.6% and sleep count 20 labelled 15.2%, inconsistent with n=76; female-pain percentage absent
Overall YGTSS SD 16.00 incompatible with sex-partition summaries; no corrected quantity selected
Ambiguous percentage denominator and domain-score formula; do not reconstruct respondent-level domains. Additional score-sum discrepancy noted by independent review

HTML/XML renders several coefficient symbols as p while PDF resembles rho; coefficient/encoding ambiguity rather than verified exact p-values. Positive 0.441 conflicts with inverse-direction prose. Do not repair sign or significance.
No subscale-scoring definition sufficient to verify relative importance from raw totals; external range concern remains version-dependent

uncertainty.reported: Means/SDs, medians, selected ranges, rounded p-values and Spearman coefficients/significance symbols
uncertainty.unavailable: Confidence intervals for prevalence, pain differences/correlations, care usefulness or effects; paired covariance; counts by severe-pain category; present-pain-positive count; corrected help-seeking denominator; duration-defined pain and benefit
uncertainty.not_computed: No confidence interval, paired test, treatment effect, equivalence bound, clinically important threshold, respondent-level reconstruction or causal mediation

ethics_funding_data.ethics: Bioethics Committee of the Regional Medical Chamber of Gdańsk, Poland; written informed consent reported
ethics_funding_data.conflicts: Author reports no commercial/financial relationship construed as conflict
ethics_funding_data.data_access: Author availability-on-request statement, not granted access; only blank questionnaire supplement retrieved, no participant data requested or used

privacy: Original aggregate extraction only; no participant quotations, singleton values, raw paper, individual/family data or participant records in deliverables
